# Lifecycle and Concurrency Checklist: Safe Automatic Updates

**Purpose**: Formally review whether safe-idle/drain and atomic activation/recovery requirements are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before implementation
**Created**: 2026-10-23
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all forms of admitted or automatically resumable work that prevent safe idle explicitly enumerated, including running, retry, quota-waiting, workflow continuation, automatic review, and merge-queue activity? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the specification define which newly eligible work is blocked during drain and which already admitted continuations remain allowed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements present for canceling drain and releasing dispatch when updating is disabled, a candidate is abandoned, or preparation fails? [Gap, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK004 Are startup and restart requirements defined for pending candidates, stale locks, prepared worktrees, and authoritative running revision discovery? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK005 Are the responsibilities of the service, activation helper, launcher, and external supervisor fully bounded across shutdown, mutation, restart, and recovery? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-017]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is “safely quiescent” defined as an atomic decision rather than a snapshot assembled from independently changing status surfaces? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the exact point at which a candidate becomes admitted for activation distinguished from detection, preparation, pending, and draining states? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK008 Is “preserve or restore a runnable prior installation” defined clearly enough to determine which artifact is retained and who starts it after failure? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK009 Are “same repository,” “clean checkout,” “attached default branch,” and “fast-forward” constraints stated consistently across eligibility and activation requirements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the bounded retry/reporting expectation for source unavailability distinguished from the blocked outcome for deterministic preparation or activation failures? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-012]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Do drain requirements preserve the root specification’s retry, quota continuation, automatic-review, and merge-queue lifecycle semantics without creating a second owner of issue state? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK012 Are immutable-SHA admission, moved-branch invalidation, and exact-SHA activation requirements mutually consistent? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK013 Do dynamic-disable requirements agree with the rule that an activation already handed off must not be interrupted into an unsafe partial state? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK014 Are source-checkout-only scope boundaries consistent across functional requirements, assumptions, configuration fields, and operator documentation obligations? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016, Spec §Assumptions]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Can uninterrupted admitted work be objectively observed for every lifecycle category named by safe-idle requirements? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK016 Does the activation deadline identify a measurable start point and account for configuration reload, preparation duration, supervisor restart, and health confirmation? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK017 Are “reconcilable after startup” and the evidence required for workspace, checkpoint, quota, review, and merge-queue recovery objectively defined? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK018 Can preservation of operator files and repository history be evaluated for every dirty, detached, divergent, concurrent, and failure scenario? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the disabled-mode observation criterion explicit about reload timing and all update-source request and installation-mutation paths? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-006]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for a candidate changing while preparation or drain is in progress, including invalidation of old evidence and drain-token ownership? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK021 Are simultaneous interval ticks, manual/status calls, configuration reloads, and a second local service process covered by one serialization requirement? [Coverage, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK022 Are failure requirements complete for interruption before old-process exit, after exit but before checkout mutation, during fast-forward/install, and after restart launch? [Gap, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK023 Are stale lock ownership, lock-holder death, and safe operator recovery requirements specified without permitting destructive cleanup? [Gap, Spec §FR-010, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements present for a newly dispatchable issue arriving at the same moment quiescence is evaluated? [Coverage, Race Condition, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-008]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK025 Are secret-redaction and bounded-diagnostic requirements applied consistently to Git command output, helper failures, paths, configuration, logs, and status surfaces? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK026 Are non-overlap and no-delay expectations stated measurably enough to prevent update checks from degrading normal issue polling? [Gap, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK027 Does the specification require one canonical update snapshot for terminal, JSON, and LiveView surfaces to prevent observational drift? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK028 Are the required capabilities and failure contract of Git, Mise, the launcher, and the external supervisor explicitly documented as deployment dependencies? [Dependency, Spec §FR-016, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK029 Is the assumption that the configured Git remote can advertise the default branch validated or paired with a defined failure outcome? [Assumption, Spec §FR-002, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the single-installation filesystem-lock assumption clearly separated from out-of-scope multi-node coordination? [Assumption, Spec §FR-010, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
